title: After a year in storage, Santa always tests out the ol' sleigh the month before
summary: Matt Frank went out along Chelsea Creek last night to capture the full moon and the Tobin, when what to his wondering eyes did appear, but a honking big sleigh and eight big ol' reindeer - atop the Chelsea salt pile. title: Man convicted for shooting motorcyclist to death on I-93 in 2017, but acquitted of murdering his girlfriend at his mom's home the same day
summary: A Suffolk Superior Court jury yesterday convicted Lance Holloman, 39, of Dorchester for shooting two motorcyclists, one fatally, on I-93 on Sept. 10, 2017, but acquitted him for the gunshot murder of his girlfriend about five hours later at his mother's house about two miles away, the Suffolk County District Attorney's office reports. Holloman will be formally sentenced on Jan. 7, but the first-degree murder conviction means an automatic sentence of life without parole. He was also convicted of two counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon and armed assault to murder, according to court records. Scott Stevens, Jr., 32, and his father, Scott Stevens, Sr., were riding their motorcycles on I-93 south just before Neponset Circle shortly after 5 p.m. when somebody shot them from what police said was a rented Jeep. The younger man, shot in the head, died, his father, shot in the shoulder, survived. Around 10:20 that night, police found Holloman's girlfriend, Michaela Gingras, 24, shot to death at 11 Santuit St. in Dorchester - owned by Holloman's mother Daphne. Police said her body had been moved and the area where she had been shot showed evidence of an attempt at cleaning. Two days later, police in Franklin found Hollomon by the side of the road, screaming . He was transported back to Boston for arraignment on an unrelated incident a few months before the shootings, in which he allegedly directed another person to throw a loaded handgun from a vehicle while fleeing a traffic stop - even as he was already facing charges for assault and battery and animal cruelty. The same day in 2017 that Holloman was indicted in Suffolk Superior Court, his mother Daphne, his sister Latoya and the mother of his child, Boston Police Officer Monicka Stinson, were all indicted on charges of misleading investigators. The case against Daphne Holloman was dismissed in June, 2021. The case against Latoya Holloman remains open - she's next scheduled for a court appearance on Jan. 5. Stinson, a ten-year BPD veteran, was suspended from the force for failing to tell investigators that Holloman had called her at least three times after the shootings. On May 13 of this year, she pleaded guilty and was sentenced to a year of probation.
